🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A South Carolina father was arrested Friday after police say he left his 6-year-old daughter sleeping alone outside a Target store so she could hold his place in line for a new Pokémon card release.

John-Michael Dooley, 35, of Johns Island, was charged with unlawful conduct toward a child, the Charleston Police Department said. Officers responded around 2:30 a.m. Friday to the Target in the city's West Ashley neighborhood after reports of an unattended child.

Police say Dooley had been waiting in line with his daughter for the release of the new Pokémon Trading Card Game expansion, "Mega Evolution — Delta Reign," which went on sale Friday. Witnesses told officers that sometime after 1 a.m., Dooley gave his daughter a pillow and a blanket, then left her asleep in line and went home.

Dooley later returned to the store, where witnesses identified him to officers, and he was arrested. According to police, he told detectives he went home and left his daughter in line because he was afraid he would lose his place and miss the chance to buy the cards.

The girl was unharmed. She was placed in emergency protective custody with the South Carolina Department of Social Services.

Dooley was booked into the Al Cannon Detention Center, and his bond was set at $40,000.

The charge is an allegation, and Dooley is presumed innocent until proven guilty in court.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar); USA Today; Charleston Police Department.
